Why GraphRAG Isn't Enough: Double-Entry Bookkeeping for Codebases

AFWE Core Architecture Team • October 24, 2026 • 6 min read

Current developer tooling relies on a single premise: if you feed an LLM enough relevant context snippets from the codebase, it will produce code that respects your architecture.

In practice, this model breaks down. Code search, AST query tools, and GraphRAG can tell an agent what your codebase is at this exact second. They cannot tell the agent what your code was supposed to be.

The Accounting Defect in AI Coding

For five hundred years, accountants have not relied on a single ledger. Single-entry bookkeeping is prone to silent fraud, missing entries, and drift. To prevent errors, double-entry bookkeeping requires every credit to balance an offsetting debit.

AFWE applies double-entry bookkeeping to software:

  • Ledger 1 (The Implementation): The actual physical source code in your repository, parsed via Tree-sitter.
  • Ledger 2 (The Intent & Memory): The declared AST claims, active pins, and geometric boundary constraints in .afwe/.

Verification at the Commit Boundary

When an agent finishes editing files, AFWE does not ask an LLM if the change looks good. A deterministic Rust kernel checks every declared claim and invariant rule. If an agent silently dropped a checkout payment method or violated an architectural boundary, the turn gate returns a REDO with structured leaf-to-root diagnostics.
